newsitem.title: UK: Shell tumbles on Nigerian output concerns.
newsitem.headline: Shell tumbles on Nigerian output concerns.

text.p: Shares in Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc tumbled by more than two percent on Monday amid concerns about an output disruption in Nigeria, traders said.
Earlier, the oil giant said it was losing 100,000 barrels of crude oil per day after shutting down on Saturday six flow stations because of a feud between two villages.
And though the company said the closure was not affecting crude exports, Shell shares sank 24-1/2p to 1056-1/2 by 1421 GMT.
Shell produces almost half of Nigeria's two million barrels per day of crude oil.
"Nigeria is a bit of a problem child for Shell. But these feuds are nothing new," said Jurjen Lunshof, an analyst with Credit Lyonnais Laing.
"I think the market is fretting more than is merited and brokers are just scratching around for business," added Lunshof, who maintains a "hold" rating on the stock.

Dealers said weak oil prices also contributed to the decline, yet shares in Burmah Castrol Plc climbed 21p to 1003-1/2 as brokerage ABN AMRO Hoare Govett upgraded the stock to "undervalued" from "hold."
